Appreciate the detail, Alex — this is perfect. I ran a quick back-of-envelope using the prompt sample and the volume you shared to show how prefix caching + commitment affects the effective $/1M tokens. Below are concise scenarios; I’ll follow up with a spreadsheet that breaks down assumptions line-by-line.

Assumptions (quick):
- List (Hosted) price for the model variant used in demo: $2,000 per 1M tokens.
- Dedicated (committed) discount: 25% off list at a baseline commit level we can size for you (see note on committing below).
- Cache behavior: we assume cache hit reduces billed tokens roughly proportional to hit rate (prefix cache hits avoid recomputing the cached prefix tokens). This is a simplified model — we’ll refine when we have full token logs.

Effective $/1M tokens under hit-rate scenarios:

Hosted (no commit):
- 0% hit: $2,000 per 1M
- 10% hit: $1,800 per 1M
- 35% hit: $1,300 per 1M
- 60% hit: $800 per 1M

Dedicated (25% commit discount applied to base):
- 0% hit: $1,500 per 1M
- 10% hit: $1,350 per 1M
- 35% hit: $975 per 1M
- 60% hit: $600 per 1M

Interpretation: with the 60% prefix-hit scenario, a Dedicated commit (25% discount) gets you well inside the $400–$700 target band (we show $600). At mid 35% hit you’re around $975 on Dedicated — closer but still above your top target. Hosted alone only approaches the range at unrealistically high hit rates or with additional promotional credits.

Commit sizing note: to achieve the 25% commit discount we’d target a monthly committed spend that we can size against your monthly token run-rate; I’ll include a small sensitivity table in the spreadsheet that shows the commit level required to reach 25% and the implied effective $/1M at each hit rate.

Next steps I suggest: 
1) We’ll run the detailed worksheet (attached: cache-sensitivity-modeling.xlsx) using the prompt-sample.txt you shared and your monthly volume to generate per-token billed reductions and a commit recommendation.
2) If the 60% hit looks realistic after the deeper run, we’ll produce a Dedicated quote (redwood-quote-dedicated-v2.pdf) and a short Mutually Agreed Plan that aligns procurement milestones to contract signatures.
3) Quick 30-minute sync next week to walk the sheet and where to land on commit size. 

If you want, I can also run an intermediate 45% scenario in the sheet — happy to add that.

Thanks — I’ll get the first-pass spreadsheet to you within 48 hours.
